- When sentiment is positive (≥0.4) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2–4% above peak for next 7–14 days.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.2) and price is trending up, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast for next 3–7 days.  
- Model consistently underestimates in early forecast windows (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) when sentiment is neutral or slightly negative; apply +0.5–1.5% bias for short-term (1–3d) forecasts.  
- Mean reversion bias: if price is above 30-day moving average for 3+ days, model often overestimates; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 5–10 days.  
- Sentiment spikes (≥0.4) in last 3–5 days correlate with 3–5 day price acceleration; model often fails to capture this; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% for next 3–5 days.
